test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which part of the Indian Constitution is related with the Panchayats?
solution:
The correct answer is __**IX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Panchayati Raj in India**

 
 
• In contrast to urban and suburban municipalities,** villages in rural India are governed locally through the Panchayati Raj **(Council of Five Officials) system.
 
• It comprises of the **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**, which enable villages to practice self-government.
 
• Their mission is to **"strengthen social justice, advance economic growth, and implement Central and State Government Schemes**, including those 29 issues stated in the Eleventh Schedule." 
 
• The provision of the Indian Constitution that deals with Panchayats is **Part IX**.
 
• It indicates that there are** three levels of PRIs in states or Union Territories with more than two million residents**:
 
 
• the **Mandal Parishad, Block Samiti, or Panchayat Samiti** at the block level
 
• the **Gram Panchayats** at the village level and
 
• the **Zila Parishad** at the district level.
 
 
 
• There are only **two levels of PRIs** in states or Union Territories with **less than two million residents**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every** five years**, members of the Panchayats at all levels are **elected**.
 
• **Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs)** must be represented in the Panchayats in an equal number to the general population.
 
• **Women** must hold at least **one-third of all seats and chairperson positions**, and in **some states, up to 50%** of all seats and chairperson positions.
 
• The **historical Panchayati raj system of the Indian subcontinent**, which is also present in Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Nepal, served as the basis for the **current Panchayati Raj system**, which was first implemented in India by the **73rd constitutional amendment in 1992**.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system is **currently exist in all states with the exception of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram**, as well as in all **Union Territories with the exception of Delhi**.
